title: BackLink
summary: Going back is the system back gesture and the navigation icon of the top app bar. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Put a MonarchIconButton with a back arrow in the navigationIcon slot of the TopAppBar of every screen below the top level; its onClick navigates up. Use BackHandler only to intercept system back, for example to confirm discarding unsaved changes.
whenNotToUse: Do not put a "Back to …" link in the content of a screen; the top app bar and the system gesture already go back. Do not use BackHandler to block back without telling the person why.
api: @Composable fun TopAppBar(title: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, navigationIcon: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {}, ...)

@Composable fun MonarchIconButton(label: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, loadingLabel: String? = null, shape: Shape? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, icon: @Composable () -> Unit)
@Composable fun BackHandler(enabled: Boolean = true, onBack: () -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchIcon(painter: Painter, contentDescription: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchIconSize = MonarchIconSize.Md, tint: Color = LocalContentColor.current, mirrorInRtl: Boolean = false)
appearance: The top app bar and its icon button use the Material 3 colors mapped from the Monarch theme. The arrow is the app's icon, mirrored in a right-to-left layout.
platformNotes: The web BackLink is a link in the page content with a leading arrow, a variant and its own text ("Back to domains"). On Android back is owned by the system: the back gesture and button, with predictive back, and the navigation icon of the top app bar. The arrow has no visible text; its content description is "Back" or "Navigate up" in the app's strings, and the screen's title in the bar tells people where they are. The web's variant has no equivalent. Monarch bundles no icons, so the app passes the arrow and mirrors it with mirrorInRtl = true or an auto-mirrored vector. iOS uses the NavigationStack back button.
accessibility: The navigation icon is a MonarchIconButton: one TalkBack button named by the icon's content description, with a 48dp touch target.
System back works with TalkBack's back gesture as well.
The arrow must point to the start: mirror it in a right-to-left layout.
edgeCases: On the top-level screen there is no navigation icon; back leaves the app.
An enabled BackHandler takes system back from the screens below it until it is disabled.

examples.title: Confirming before discarding unsaved changes
examples.code:
BackHandler(enabled = unsaved) { confirming = true }
MonarchText(text = if (confirming) "Discard your changes?" else "Editing. Press back to leave.")
examples.setup:
val unsaved = true
var confirming by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

parityExceptions.reason: there is no BackLink component; going up is the system back button of the navigation stack (iOS) or the top app bar navigation icon (Android). The template draws each link as a ghost button with a leading chevron; the web's default and standalone variants (muted and accent text) are not expressed
parityExceptions.convention: going up is the top app bar navigation icon and the system back gesture, not a link in the content
